checks.name: Single source
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --test compat; cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --doc compat
checks.output: 23/23 compatibility tests and both R1-17 doctests pass. automonique_registry generates the checked-in module for 4 entries, 8 spellings and 4 aliases; byte drift is tested, and the compile-fail doctest proves an undeclared LegacyName constant is unavailable.

checks.name: Forwarding only
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --test compat forwarding_only; cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --test compat generated_from_the_registry
checks.output: 2 forwarding tests and 6 real-generation tests pass. Every generated alias resolves to the same NameEntry, owner and durable identity as its canonical spelling; LegacyAlias carries only spelling, authorization and retirement metadata and exports no behavior path.

checks.name: Conflict rejection
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --test compat conflict_rejection
checks.output: 3/3 conflict tests pass. Canonical plus alias is a typed CanonicalAndAliasBothSet error naming both spellings and values, independent of order and even when values agree; resolution contains no precedence path.

checks.name: Deprecation observation
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --test compat deprecation_observation
checks.output: 2/2 observation tests pass. Alias-only configuration returns an enumerable DeprecationObservation with canonical destination and retirement window; canonical-only configuration returns no deprecation observation.

checks.name: One owner
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --test compat one_owner; cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --test compat the_declared_registry -- --nocapture
checks.output: 2/2 owner tests pass and the production table reports 4 entries, 8 spellings and 4 aliases. Every row agrees on owner and durable identity, exactly one spelling per entry is canonical, and a second owner is rejected.

checks.name: Authorized aliases
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --test compat authorized_aliases
checks.output: 2/2 authorization tests pass. All 4 shipped aliases carry a non-empty migration-contract citation and the 0.9.0 compatibility window; 0 shipped aliases lack either. Construction without the typed contract value is unavailable.

checks.name: Identifier location
checks.output: The whole-tree identifier-location rule passes. Its checked-in negative controls and anti-vacuity checks cover the branded predecessor prefix and hand-written LEGACY_* aliases in shipped Rust source; lowercase compatibility namespace spellings remain covered by R1-19.

checks.name: Durable identifiers unchanged
checks.command: python3 tools/identifiers/inventory.py verify; python3 -m unittest tools.identifiers.test_inventory.ConsumerContract -v; cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked --offline -p automonique-protocol --test compat durable_identifiers_unchanged
checks.output: The R0-13 inventory re-derives from 10 permitted documentation regions: 159 entries (140 durable, 17 compatibility-only, 2 presentation-only). All 3 consumer-contract tests pass: every generated canonical spelling is independently classified durable, every generated alias appears in compatibility_forwards and targets its recorded forwards_to or also spelling, and the namespace exception set is non-empty. Both rename-invariance tests pass.

checks.name: Quality
checks.command: python3 plan/check.py --verify; cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check; cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked --offline -- -D warnings; cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --locked --offline --no-fail-fast
checks.output: Plan verification, formatting, strict all-target/all-feature Clippy, and every workspace test target and doctest pass. Cargo ran locked and offline. Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock are unchanged, no dependency was added, and the pre-completion tree is otherwise clean.

review.acceptance: Independent read-only review accepted all 9 rows at the admitted base and found no product-code change necessary. It independently measured 23/23 compatibility tests, both relevant doctests, all 3 R0-13 consumer comparisons, the 4-entry/8-spelling/4-alias generated table, inventory verification, plan verification and no manifest or lock drift.

notes: R1-17 was implemented in an earlier partial slice. Its sole open row depended on R0-13; that inventory is now integrated and its explicit one-way consumer contract passes against the real generated registry, so this transaction records completion without changing product code. Proof scope is truthful: the shipped registry contains the four aliases required by its permitted migration inputs, not every one of R0-13's 17 compatibility-only path/package/command entries; R0-13 requires membership and correct forwarding rather than set equality. MigrationContract validates a bounded non-empty citation value, while the shipped citations' actual authority was confirmed by review of permitted documents. No durable name, live configuration, data, runtime behavior, manifest, lockfile or licence boundary changed.
